description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:251-266

CURRENT IMPL:
    pub fn seed_object(
        &self,
        account_id: &str,
        type_name: &'static str,
        id: &str,
        value: serde_json::Value,
    ) {
        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
        inner.known_accounts.insert(account_id.to_owned());
        inner
            .objects_mut(type_name, account_id)
            .insert(Id::from(id), value);
        if type_name == "ContactCard" {
            inner.recompute_address_books_with_contents(account_id);
        }
    }

PROBLEM:
The function accepts ANY serde_json::Value without validating it
deserializes into the type named by `type_name`. Common failure modes:

1. Missing required fields. Seeding `json!({"id": "ab1"})` as an
   AddressBook is accepted; subsequent `get_objects::<AddressBook>`
   call fails with `MemoryError("deserialize AddressBook: ...")` at
   memory.rs:362. The error surface is far from the seeding call site;
   the test author debugs the wrong layer.

2. Type-name typo. Seeding under `"Addressbook"` (lowercase 'b') —
   accepted, stored in a bucket no get_objects call ever reads.
   See JMAP-qz9v.24 for the stringly-typed-parameter angle.

3. Schema drift. Seeding fixtures written for an earlier ContactCard
   schema (e.g., before a `@type` field was required). The fixture
   sits silently mis-shaped until a deserialize attempt.

This forces every test author to write defensive checks AROUND
seed_object:

    let v = json!({ ... });
    let _check: AddressBook = serde_json::from_value(v.clone())
        .expect("fixture shape is valid");
    backend.seed_object("acc1", "AddressBook", "ab1", v);

— which is exactly the defensive boilerplate the prompt section
"Defensive-code-forcing" is designed to prevent.

WHAT EVERY CALLER WILL DO:
- Either skip validation and debug stale fixtures one-by-one when a
  test fails late, or
- Re-implement the typed validation manually at every seed call site.

RECOMMENDED:
Validate at seed time. Two equivalent forms:

(a) Typed signature (see JMAP-qz9v.33):
        pub fn seed<O: JmapObject + Serialize>(
            &self, account_id: &Id, id: &Id, obj: &O
        )
    — no Value passed; the type system guarantees shape.

(b) Validate-on-insert in the current Value-based signature:
        let typed_check: serde_json::Result<...> = match type_name {
            "AddressBook" => from_value::<AddressBook>(value.clone()).map(|_| ()),
            "ContactCard" => from_value::<ContactCard>(value.clone()).map(|_| ()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown type_name: {other}")),
        };
        typed_check.map_err(|e| format!("invalid fixture: {e}"))?;
    Return Result instead of unit; force callers to handle the error
    at the call site.

(a) is strictly better — it puts validation in the type system.

P2 because the failure mode is "test debugging time wasted" rather
than runtime bug, but the test suite is the audience this helper is
designed to serve, and the design actively works against that
audience.
title: MemoryBackend::seed_object accepts any serde_json::Value — invalid fixtures fail-late at get_objects, not at seed time
